classification.difficultyReason: Convert already ordered observations to two displays, omit the central value for quartiles and apply IQR fences to distinguish outliers from whisker endpoints; then interpret the upper tail. Number of observations increases workload rather than reasoning demand.

inlines.text: The following data are the speeds of 45 semi-trailers passing a given point on an interstate highway. The speeds are measured in km/h.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct a dotplot of the data.

answer.worked: Use a horizontal speed scale in km/h. Place one dot for each semi-trailer above its speed, stacking dots vertically for repeated speeds. There are 45 dots in total.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 data and part a; teacher PDF page 86 bottom dotplot
spec.description: Complete dotplot with all 45 observations; ordinary marks are black under house style.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Construct a boxplot of the data.

answer.short: $Q_1=100$, median $=106$, $Q_3=117.5$ km/h. Whiskers end at $88$ and $141$ km/h; outliers are $144$ and $150$ km/h.
answer.worked:
There are 45 ordered values. The median is the 23rd value, $106$ km/h. Omit this value and split the remaining data into two groups of 22.

$$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{100+100}{2}\\Q_1&=100\text{ km/h}\\Q_3&=\frac{117+118}{2}\\Q_3&=117.5\text{ km/h}\\\mathrm{IQR}&=117.5-100\\\mathrm{IQR}&=17.5\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Lower fence}&=100-1.5(17.5)\\\text{Lower fence}&=73.75\text{ km/h}\\\text{Upper fence}&=117.5+1.5(17.5)\\\text{Upper fence}&=143.75\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

The values $144$ and $150$ km/h exceed the upper fence. Draw the box from $100$ to $117.5$, mark the median at $106$, and extend the whiskers to the lowest and highest non-outliers, $88$ and $141$ km/h. Mark $144$ and $150$ separately.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 part b; teacher PDF page 86 bottom boxplot
spec.description: Modified boxplot with black outlines and separate triangular outlier markers. Right whisker corrected to highest non-outlier 141.
spec.mathematics: Q1=100, median=106, Q3=117.5; whiskers 88 and 141; outliers 144 and 150.

answer.short: Positively skewed, with a long tail towards higher speeds.
answer.worked: Most speeds cluster around $100$–$120$ km/h, while a few larger values extend the right-hand tail towards $150$ km/h. The distribution is positively skewed.
